text:
Predicates:
TwinOrTriplet(x) ::: x is either a twin or triplet.
SpendTimeWithSiblings(x) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with and playing with siblings.
SameAgeSiblings(x, y) ::: x has siblings who are the same age as y.
ComplainsOften(x, y) ::: x complains often about y.
LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) ::: x lives at home regularly.
DevelopsStrongBonds(x) ::: x develops strong bonds with family members.
Siblings(x, y) ::: x and y are siblings.

Premises:
∀x (TwinOrTriplet(x) → SpendTimeWithSiblings(x)) ::: If people are twins or triplets, then they spend a lot of time with siblings.
∀x ∀y (SameAgeSiblings(x, y) → TwinOrTriplet(x)) ::: If people have siblings who are the same age, then they are twins or triplets.
∀x (ComplainsOften(x, siblings) → SameAgeSiblings(x, y)) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who are the same age.
¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) → ¬DevelopsStrongBonds(x) ::: If people do not live at home regularly, then they do not develop strong bonds.
SpendTimeWithSiblings(x) → ¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) ::: If people spend a lot of time with siblings, then they often did not live at home regularly.
Conclusion:
ComplainsOften(luke, siblings) ::: Luke complains often about annoying siblings.
